narrative:
The model estimates a 32% chance that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is a material risk: roughly one in three students with a similar profile would not pass, so the school is treating your case as requiring remedial courses rather than waiting until the end of the year.

The strongest signal was your intention not to continue into higher education; in the comparison group, every student who passed wanted to continue, so this was the largest push toward failing. The second most influential factor was your reason for choosing the school being home; this was the only top factor working in your favour, nudging the prediction toward passing. The third was your one past class failure, compared with an average of none among students who passed, which increased the concern. Other context reinforces it: you study less than two hours a week, while most passers study two to five, and you have eight absences against an average of about four.

To improve your position, use the remedial courses as structured support and speak with your counsellor about whether continuing education is a realistic goal and what help would make it possible. Address the past failure pattern by seeking help early, increasing weekly study time, and reducing absences.
